readings.title: The Law of the Red Heifer
readings.subtitle: Water for Cleansing
readings.text: [Numbers 19:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, saying, [2] <dq>“This is a law of the Torah which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has commanded, saying, ‘Speak to the children of Yisra’el, that they bring you a red heifer, a perfect one, in which there is no blemish, and on which a yoke has never come.</dq> [3] <dq>‘And you shall give it to El’azar the priest, and he shall bring it outside the camp, and it shall be slaughtered before him.</dq> [4] <dq>‘And El’azar the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger, and sprinkle some of its blood seven times directly in front of the Tent of Appointment.</dq> [5] <dq>‘And the heifer shall be burned before his eyes: its hide, and its flesh, and its blood, with its dung, shall be burned.</dq> [6] <dq>‘And the priest shall take cedar wood and hyssop and scarlet, and throw them into the midst of the fire burning the heifer.</dq> [7] <dq>‘The priest shall then wash his garments, and shall bathe his body in water, and afterward he comes into the camp, but the priest is unclean until evening.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And he who burns it washes his garments in water, and bathes his body in water, and is unclean until evening.</dq> [9] <dq>‘And a clean man shall gather up the ashes of the heifer, and shall place them outside the camp in a clean place. And they shall be kept for the congregation of the children of Yisra’el for the water for uncleanness, it is for cleansing from sin.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And he who gathers the ashes of the heifer shall wash his garments, and is unclean until evening. And it shall be a law forever to the children of Yisra’el and to the stranger who sojourns in their midst.</dq> [11] <dq>‘He who touches the dead of any human life is unclean for seven days.</dq> [12] <dq>‘He cleanses himself with the water on the third day and on the seventh day, then he is clean. But if he does not cleanse himself on the third day and on the seventh day, he is not clean.</dq> [13] <dq>‘Anyone who touches the dead of a human life that has died, and does not cleanse himself, defiles the Dwelling Place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And that being shall be cut off from Yisra’el. Because the water for uncleanness was not sprinkled on him, he is unclean – his uncleanness is still upon him.</dq> [14] <dq>‘This is the Torah when a man dies in a tent: All who come into the tent and all who are in the tent are unclean for seven days.</dq> [15] <dq>‘And every open vessel, which has no cover fastened on it, is unclean.</dq> [16] <dq>‘And anyone in the open field who touches one who is slain by a sword or who has died, or a bone of a man, or a grave, is unclean for seven days.</dq> [17] <dq>‘And for the unclean being they shall take some of the ashes of the fuel of the cleansing from sin, and running water shall be put on them in a vessel.</dq> [18] <dq>‘And a clean man shall take hyssop and dip it in the water, and shall sprinkle it on the tent, and on all the vessels, and on the beings who were there, and on the one who touched a bone, or the slain, or the dead, or a grave.</dq> [19] <dq>‘And the clean one shall sprinkle on the unclean on the third day and on the seventh day. And on the seventh day he shall cleanse himself, and shall wash his garments and bathe in water, and shall be clean in the evening.</dq> [20] <dq>‘But the man who is unclean and does not cleanse himself, that being shall be cut off from the midst of the assembly, because he has defiled the set-apart place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – the water for uncleanness has not been sprinkled on him, he is unclean.</dq> [21] <dq>‘And it shall be a law forever for them. And he who sprinkles the water for uncleanness washes his garments. And he who touches the water for uncleanness is unclean until evening.</dq> [22] <dq>‘And whatever the unclean being touches becomes unclean. And the being who touches it is unclean until evening.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Waters of Meriḇah
readings.subtitle: Failure at the Rock
readings.text: [Numbers 20:1] And the children of Yisra’el, all the congregation, came into the Wilderness of Tsin in the first month, and the people stayed in Qaḏesh. And Miryam died there and was buried there. [2] And there was no water for the congregation, so they assembled against Mosheh and against Aharon. [3] And the people contended with Mosheh and spoke, saying, “If only we had died when our brothers died before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! [4] “Why have you brought the assembly of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> into this wilderness, that we and our livestock should die here? [5] “And why have you brought us up out of Mitsrayim, to bring us to this evil place? Not a place of grain or figs or vines or pomegranates, and there is no water to drink.” [6] Then Mosheh and Aharon went from the presence of the assembly to the door of the Tent of Appointment, and they fell on their faces. And the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to them. [7] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [8] <dq>“Take the rod, and assemble the congregation, you and your brother Aharon. And you shall speak to the rock before their eyes, and it shall give its water. And you shall bring water for them out of the rock, and give the congregation and their livestock to drink.”</dq> [9] And Mosheh took the rod from before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, as <dn>He</dn> commanded him. [10] And Mosheh and Aharon assembled the assembly before the rock. And he said to them, “Hear now, you rebels, shall we bring water for you out of this rock?” [11] Then Mosheh lifted up his hand and struck the rock twice with his rod. And much water came out, and the congregation and their livestock drank. [12] But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, <dq>“Because you did not believe <dn>Me</dn>, to set <dn>Me</dn> apart in the eyes of the children of Yisra’el, therefore you do not bring this assembly into the land which <dn>I</dn> have given them.”</dq> [13] These were the waters of Meriḇah, because the children of Yisra’el contended with <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> was set-apart among them.

readings.title: Passage Refused
readings.subtitle: Edom's Resistance
readings.text: [Numbers 20:14] And Mosheh sent messengers from Qaḏesh to the sovereign of Eḏom, “This is what your brother Yisra’el said, ‘You know all the hardship that has befallen us, [15] ‘that our fathers went down to Mitsrayim, and we dwelt in Mitsrayim a long time, and the Mitsrites did evil to us and our fathers. [16] ‘And we cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> heard our voice and sent a Messenger and brought us up out of Mitsrayim. And see, we are in Qaḏesh, a city on the edge of your border. [17] ‘Please let us pass through your land. We shall not pass through fields or vineyards, nor drink water from wells. We shall go along the sovereign’s highway, we shall not turn aside to the right or to the left until we have passed through your border.’ ” [18] But Eḏom said to him, “You do not pass through me, lest I come out against you with the sword.” [19] And the children of Yisra’el said to him, “We shall go up by the highway, and if I or my livestock drink any of your water, then I shall pay for it. Let me only pass through on my feet, nothing more.” [20] But he said, “You do not pass through.” And Eḏom came out against them with many people and with a strong hand. [21] So Eḏom refused to let Yisra’el pass through his border. And Yisra’el turned away from him.

readings.title: The Death of Aharon
readings.subtitle: Passing the Mantle
readings.text: [Numbers 20:22] And the children of Yisra’el, all the congregation, set out from Qaḏesh and came to Mount Hor. [23] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon in Mount Hor by the border of the land of Eḏom, saying, [24] <dq>“Aharon is to be gathered to his people, for he is not to enter the land which <dn>I</dn> have given to the children of Yisra’el, because you rebelled against <dn>My</dn> mouth at the water of Meriḇah.</dq> [25] <dq>Take Aharon and El’azar his son, and bring them up to Mount Hor,</dq> [26] <dq>and strip Aharon of his garments and put them on El’azar his son, for Aharon is to be gathered to his people and die there.”</dq> [27] And Mosheh did as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded, and they went up to Mount Hor in the eyes of all the congregation. [28] And Mosheh stripped Aharon of his garments and put them on El’azar his son. And Aharon died there on the top of the mountain. And Mosheh and El’azar came down from the mountain. [29] And all the congregation saw that Aharon was dead, and they wept for Aharon thirty days, all the house of Yisra’el.

readings.title: Victory at Ḥormah
readings.subtitle: A Vow to YeHoVaH
readings.text: [Numbers 21:1] And the Kena’anite, the sovereign of Araḏ, who dwelt in the South, heard that Yisra’el was coming by the way of Atharim, and he fought against Yisra’el and took some of them captive. [2] Then Yisra’el made a vow to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, “If <dn>You</dn> deliver this people into my hand, then I shall put their cities under the ban.” [3] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> listened to the voice of Yisra’el and gave up the Kena’anites, and they put them and their cities under the ban. So the name of that place was called Ḥormah.

readings.title: The Bronze Serpent
readings.subtitle: Looking to Live
readings.text: [Numbers 21:4] And they set out from Mount Hor by the way of the Sea of Reeds, to go around the land of Eḏom. And the soul of the people became impatient because of the way. [5] And the people spoke against <dn>Elohim</dn> and against Mosheh, “Why have you brought us up out of Mitsrayim to die in the wilderness? For there is no food and no water, and our soul loathes this light bread.” [6] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people. And many of the people of Yisra’el died. [7] Then the people came to Mosheh and said, “We have sinned, for we have spoken against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and against you. Pray to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to take away the serpents from us.” So Mosheh prayed for the people. [8] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Make a fiery serpent, and set it on a pole. And it shall be that everyone who is bitten, when he looks at it, shall live.”</dq> [9] So Mosheh made a bronze serpent, and put it on a pole. And it came to be, if a serpent had bitten anyone, and he looked at the bronze serpent, he lived.

readings.title: The Journey Continues
readings.subtitle: The Valley of Mo'aḇ
readings.text: [Numbers 21:10] And the children of Yisra’el set out and camped in Oḇoth. [11] And they set out from Oḇoth and camped at Iyye Ha-Aḇarim, in the wilderness which is east of Mo’aḇ, toward the sunrise. [12] From there they set out and camped in the wadi Zereḏ. [13] From there they set out and camped on the other side of the Arnon, which is in the wilderness that comes out of the border of the Amorites. For the Arnon is the border of Mo’aḇ, between Mo’aḇ and the Amorites. [14] Therefore it is said in the Book of the Battles of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Waheḇ in Suphah, and the wadis of the Arnon, [15] and the slope of the wadis that reaches to the dwelling of Ar, and leans on the border of Mo’aḇ.” [16] And from there they went to Be’ēr, which is the well where <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Assemble the people, and <dn>I</dn> give them water.”</dq> [17] Then Yisra’el sang this song, “Rise up, O well! Sing to it! [18] “A well dug by leaders, hollowed out by the noble of the people, with a lawgiver, with their staffs.” And from the wilderness they went to Mattanah, [19] and from Mattanah to Naḥali’el, and from Naḥali’el to Bamoth, [20] and from Bamoth to the valley that is in the country of Mo’aḇ, to the top of Pisgah, which looks down on the wasteland.

readings.title: Victory Over the Amorites
readings.subtitle: The Defeat of Siḥon and Og̱
readings.text: [Numbers 21:21] And Yisra’el sent messengers to Siḥon sovereign of the Amorites, saying, [22] “Let me pass through your land. We shall not turn aside into fields or vineyards, we shall not drink water from wells. We shall go by the sovereign’s highway until we have passed through your border.” [23] But Siḥon would not allow Yisra’el to pass through his border. So Siḥon gathered all his people together and went out against Yisra’el into the wilderness, and he came to Yahats and fought against Yisra’el. [24] And Yisra’el struck him with the edge of the sword, and took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Yabboq, as far as the children of Ammon, for the border of the children of Ammon was strong. [25] And Yisra’el took all these cities, and Yisra’el dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites, in Ḥeshbon and in all its villages. [26] For Ḥeshbon was the city of Siḥon sovereign of the Amorites, who had fought against the former sovereign of Mo’aḇ, and had taken all his land from his hand as far as the Arnon. [27] Therefore those who speak in proverbs say, “Come to Ḥeshbon, let the city of Siḥon be built and established. [28] “For fire went out from Ḥeshbon, a flame from the city of Siḥon. It consumed Ar of Mo’aḇ, the lords of the heights of the Arnon. [29] “Woe to you, Mo’aḇ! You have perished, O people of Kemosh! He has given his sons as fugitives, and his daughters into captivity, to Siḥon sovereign of the Amorites. [30] “Then we shot them: Ḥeshbon has perished as far as Diḇon. And we laid waste as far as Nophaḥ, which reaches to Mĕyḏeḇa.” [31] So Yisra’el dwelt in the land of the Amorites. [32] And Mosheh sent to spy out Ya’zēr, and they took its villages and drove out the Amorites who were there. [33] And they turned and went up by the way to Bashan. And Og̱ sovereign of Bashan went out against them, he and all his people, to battle at Edre’i. [34] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Do not fear him, for <dn>I</dn> have given him into your hand, with all his people and his land. And you shall do to him as you did to Siḥon sovereign of the Amorites, who dwelt at Ḥeshbon.”</dq> [35] So they struck him, and his sons, and all his people, until no remnant was left to him. And they took possession of his land.
